query: Consider the following context: During the hot dip aluminum plating process, components such as sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates will come into long-term contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum and be corroded by the aluminum liquid, greatly reducing their service life. In that context, which material can be used for prepare parts for the dipping and plating equipment and protect the equipment from erosion, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Sialon-based ceramics used as contact components (rollers, guide plates) in a hot-dip aluminum plating line will exhibit superior corrosion resistance to molten aluminum and thereby extend the equipment’s service life.
generation.material_initial_state: Components formed from sialon-based ceramic, sintered/machined to the desired shape and surface finish.
generation.intervention: Substitute sialon-based ceramics for metallic components in the contact regions exposed to molten aluminum during plating.
generation.conditions: Hot-dip aluminum plating environment at ~650–750°C, continuous immersion over extended operational cycles.
generation.structural_mediator: Dense sialon matrix with stable Si-O-N bonds.
generation.mechanism: Sialon ceramics resist wetting by molten aluminum, minimizing corrosive reactions and chemical dissolution compared to conventional steel or Ni-based components.
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduced mass loss and negligible structural deterioration of the sialon ceramic under molten Al exposure, yielding longer component lifetime relative to standard metallic parts.
generation.baseline: Corrosion rate of steel or Ni-based alloy components in the same molten Al conditions.
generation.boundary: Applicability limited to moderate mechanical loading conditions and the thermal range typically used for hot-dip aluminum plating (~650–750°C).
generation.uncertainty: Exact lifetime improvement factor is not specified by current data, necessitating dedicated long-term testing for precise quantification.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct comparative immersion tests of standard metal components and sialon-based ceramics in a molten aluminum bath at ~700°C for extended durations, monitoring weight changes and visual damage at regular intervals.
measurements: Mass loss or gain over time
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If sialon-based ceramics show similar or higher corrosion rates, or exhibit similar deterioration to metallic controls, then the hypothesis is disproven.
